questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical skills in per-tenant policy enforcement, dynamic configuration reload, and how a sidecar can drive access control using Kubernetes-native resources.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant ACLs loaded from ConfigMaps with tenant-specific naming conventions
- Dynamic config reload and conflict resolution between cluster-wide and namespace-scoped policies
- Sidecar architecture and policy evaluation pipeline
- Kubernetes ConfigMap watch mechanisms and Informers
- End-to-end testing within a single namespace

## Code Example
```yaml
# Example policy
tenant: tenant-a
rules:
  - path: /api/v1/users/*
    methods: ["GET","POST"]
  - path: /health
    methods: ["GET"]
```

## Implementation Details

### ConfigMap Structure
The sidecar watches ConfigMaps matching the pattern `cnf.acl.{tenant}.yaml` in the tenant's namespace. Namespace-scoped overrides follow the naming convention `cnf.acl.{tenant}.override.yaml`.

### Watch Mechanism
Use a Kubernetes Informer to watch ConfigMap changes. On update, the sidecar re-parses the YAML, merges policies (namespace overrides take precedence), and updates the in-memory rule engine without pod restart.

### Conflict Resolution
When cluster-wide and namespace-scoped policies conflict, apply a merge strategy where namespace-specific rules override cluster defaults for the same path and method combination. Log conflicts for observability.

### Testing Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-test
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf.acl.tenant-a.yaml
  namespace: tenant-a-test
data:
  policy.yaml: |
    tenant: tenant-a
    rules:
      - path: /api/v1/users/*
        methods: ["GET", "POST"]
      - path: /health
        methods: ["GET"]
```

Validate by querying the /acl/status endpoint after applying the manifest to confirm rules are loaded correctly.

## Why This Is Asked

Tests policy-as-code proficiency, practical use of Gatekeeper/OPA, and ability to derive concrete manifests and validation steps for a CNF multi-tenant setup.

## Key Concepts

- OPA Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- ReadOnlyRootFilesystem, hostNetwork, and Privileged security controls
- Namespace-scoped policy targeting CNFs
- Lightweight test manifests to validate allow/deny paths

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (yaml)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: cnfnamespacesecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraint
        listKind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraintList
        plural: cnfnamespacesecurityconstraints
        singular: cnfnamespacesecurityconstraint
  targets:
  - target: admissionreviews
    rego: |
      package cnfnamespacesecurity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        some i
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.hostNetwork
        msg := "hostNetwork is forbidden for CNFs"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        not input.review.object.spec.containers
        # fallback for non-pods
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        some i
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem != true
        msg := "readOnlyRootFilesystem is required for all containers"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.object.spec.containers[i].securityContext.privileged == true
        msg := "privileged containers are disallowed"
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (yaml)
apiVersion: cnfnamespacesecurity.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: CNFNamespaceSecurityConstraint
metadata:
  name: cnf-a-security
spec:
  namespace: cnf-a
```

```yaml
# Compliant Pod (yaml)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-cnf
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
    securityContext:
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      privileged: false
      runAsNonRoot: true
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
```

```yaml
# Non-compliant Pod (yaml)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-cnf
spec:
  hostNetwork: true
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
    securityContext:
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
      privileged: true
```

## Follow-up Steps

- Apply ConstraintTemplate, Constraint, and test manifests in a single namespace and observe denial events for non-compliant pods.
- Extend with a quick kubectl patch to simulate remediation and re-validate.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates candidate understanding of tenant-scoped dynamic capability negotiation and caching in cloud-native environments, ensuring isolation and correctness at scale.

## Key Concepts

- Tenant-scoped capability registry (implemented as a CRD or ConfigMap)
- Per-tenant, TTL-based cache in the sidecar for performance optimization
- Highest common version selection using semantic versioning
- HTTP 406 Not Acceptable response when no compatible version exists; graceful default fallback
- Observability: Prometheus metrics, structured logging, and distributed tracing

## Code Example

```go
// Pseudocode for version negotiation
func negotiate(upstreamVersions []string, tenantID string) string {
    tenantVersions := registry.GetVersions(tenantID)
    allowed := intersect(upstreamVersions, tenantVersions)
    if len(allowed) == 0 {
        return DEFAULT_VERSION
    }
    return highestVersion(allowed)
}
```

## Implementation Highlights

- Extract X-TENANT-ID header in sidecar middleware
- Query central registry for tenant capabilities
- Compute intersection with upstream supported versions
- Select highest compatible version using semver comparison
- Store result in tenant-scoped cache with configurable TTL
- Return 406 if negotiation fails and no default is configured
- Emit histogram metrics for negotiation latency and cache hit rates

## Why This Is Asked
Real-world upgrades in multi-tenant CNF platforms require safe, isolated releases. This tests your ability to design rollout strategies, implement metrics-based promotion decisions, and enforce cross-tenant risk controls.

## Key Concepts
- Argo Rollouts canary strategy scoped per tenant
- Tenant isolation via labels and service mesh subsets
- Per-tenant AnalysisRun with Prometheus-based SLAs
- Rollback and auto-promotion guardrails
- Minimal CRD sketches and namespace-scoped validation

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: gateway-rollout-tenant-a
  labels:
    tenant: a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
        - setWeight: 10
        - analysis:
            templates:
              - templateName: tenant-a-analysis
        - setWeight: 30
        - analysis:
            templates:
              - templateName: tenant-a-analysis
        - setWeight: 100
      trafficRouting:
        nginx:
          stableIngress: gateway-ingress
          additionalIngressAnnotations:
            canary-by-header: X-Tenant-ID
      analysis:
        successfulRunHistoryLimit: 3
        unsuccessfulRunHistoryLimit: 3
```

## Per-Tenant AnalysisRun CRD Sketch
```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AnalysisTemplate
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-analysis
spec:
  args:
    - name: tenant-id
  metrics:
    - name: latency-sli
      interval: 1m
      successCondition: result[0] <= 100
      failureLimit: 3
      provider:
        prometheus:
          address: http://prometheus:9090
          query: |-
            histogram_quantile(0.99,
              sum(rate(gateway_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant="{{args.tenant-id}}"}[5m]))
              by (le))
    - name: error-rate-sli
      interval: 1m
      successCondition: result[0] <= 0.01
      failureLimit: 3
      provider:
        prometheus:
          address: http://prometheus:9090
          query: |-
            sum(rate(gateway_requests_total{tenant="{{args.tenant-id}},status=~"5.."}[5m]))
            /
            sum(rate(gateway_requests_total{tenant="{{args.tenant-id}}"}[5m]))
```

## One-Namespace Test Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-canary-test
  labels:
    tenant: a
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: gateway-stable
  namespace: tenant-a-canary-test
spec:
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
  selector:
    app: gateway
    role: stable
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: gateway-canary
  namespace: tenant-a-canary-test
spec:
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
  selector:
    app: gateway
    role: canary
---
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: gateway-rollout
  namespace: tenant-a-canary-test
  labels:
    tenant: a
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: gateway
          image: gateway:v2
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
  strategy:
    canary:
      canaryService: gateway-canary
      stableService: gateway-stable
      trafficRouting:
        service:
          canaryWeight: 10
      steps:
        - setWeight: 10
        - pause: {duration: 5m}
        - setWeight: 30
        - pause: {duration: 5m}
        - setWeight: 100
```

## Traffic Isolation Design
- **Service Mesh Subsets**: Each tenant gets dedicated subsets (stable/canary) in the mesh, ensuring zero cross-tenant traffic bleed
- **Tenant Labels**: All resources (Rollouts, Services, AnalysisRuns) are labeled with tenant ID for RBAC and policy enforcement
- **Network Policies**: Kubernetes NetworkPolicies restrict pod-to-pod communication to same-tenant pods only
- **Ingress Routing**: Use header-based routing (X-Tenant-ID) at the ingress to route to tenant-specific services

## Per-Tenant Metrics Collection
- Deploy tenant-scoped Prometheus instances or use Prometheus tenants
- Configure recording rules per tenant for SLI computation
- Metrics queries always include tenant filter to ensure isolation
- Store metrics with tenant label for multi-tenant querying and alerting

## Policy Enforcement
- **OPA/Gatekeeper**: Enforce that Rollouts must have tenant label and cannot modify other tenants' resources
- **Kubernetes RBAC**: Bind roles to tenant groups, limiting access to tenant-specific namespaces
- **Argo Rollouts RBAC**: Restrict Rollout/AnalysisTemplate access to tenant admins only

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests end-to-end provenance flow across cloud-native tools, including per-tenant isolation, signing with Sigstore, and Rekor integration. It also exercises API design, data modeling, and in-cluster testing patterns relevant to CNF supply chain security.

## Key Concepts

- Sigstore attestation flow and Rekor integration
- Per-tenant key management (KMS) and image provenance
- SBOM hashing and binding to image digests
- In-cluster E2E test via ServiceAccount

## Code Example

```go
// Go pseudo-structure for attestation payload
type Attestation struct {
  ImageDigest string
  SBOMHash    string
  Tenant      string
  Verdict     string
  Timestamp   time.Time
}
```

```javascript
// Pseudo API call
POST /attest { imageDigest, tenant } -> { attestationID, signature }
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you rotate tenant keys without breaking in-flight attestations?
- How would you audit and revoke attestations if a tenant is compromised?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This probes ability to implement tenant-scoped observability using a sidecar pattern, ensuring isolation of telemetry data and correct sink routing in a CNF gateway.

## Key Concepts
- Tenant-scoped telemetry and OpenTelemetry/Prometheus format
- Sidecar pattern for non-intrusive metrics augmentation
- Prometheus remote_write configuration per-tenant
- ConfigMaps for sink endpoints and TENANT_ID propagation
- RBAC, InitContainer for bootstrap, minimal namespace scoping

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal sidecar and main gateway manifest (snipped for brevity)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: cnf/gateway:latest
      - name: telemetry-sidecar
        image: telemetry-sidecar:latest
        env:
        - name: TENANT_ID
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: metadata.labels['tenant_id']
        - name: REMOTE_WRITE_URL
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: tenant-sinks
              key: sink_url
```

```yaml
# ConfigMap providing per-tenant sink URL
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: tenant-sinks
data:
  sink_url: https://tenant-a-sink.example.com/api/v1/write
```

```yaml
# One-namespace test manifest
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate or revoke sinks without downtime?
- How would you monitor for mislabelled metrics and alert on sink failures?
